newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE TO ISSUE 5, 10YR CPI-INDEX BONDS IN MAY.
newsitem.headline: GREECE TO ISSUE 5, 10YR CPI-INDEX BONDS IN MAY.

text.p: Greece will issue five- and 10-year CPI index-linked bonds in May and the finance ministry plans to raise 300 billion drachmas from the sale of these bonds in 1997, said deputy Finance Minister Nickos Christodoulakis.

"The first issue will take place in May and the securities will be made available to the investment public via a public subscription," said Christodoulakis. "The securities will be in dematerialised form."
The issue date for the first-ever CPI-linked bonds will be announced after Orthodox Easter, he said.
"The next issues will usually take place every quarter through a public subscription or auction," added Christodoulakis.
The reference CPI index for the bonds will be the official CPI index released by the National Statistics Service (NSS) in the first 10 days every month.
Both annual coupons and principal will be CPI-linked, he added.
Investors will be entitled to their initial investment even in the case of deflation, he said.
Coupons could be stripped and traded separately even on issue day provided that the face value is a multiple of 100,000 drachmas.
The index factor measuring accrued inflation for calculation purposes is equal to the ratio of the reference CPI index on settlement date over the reference CPI index on issue date, it said.
If the settlement date is the first of the month, the reference index is the CPI falling three calendar months earlier, it added.

If the settlement date is a day other than the first of the month, the reference CPI index is found by linear interpolation between the CPI falling two and three calendar months earlier, it said. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
